headline: DOE Eyes Up to 5,000 MW of Coal Projects Exempt from Moratorium
seoTitle: DOE Eyes Up to 5,000 MW Coal Capacity | FMB News
seoDescription: DOE is preparing a coal transition plan that may accelerate 3,000 to 5,000 MW of previously committed coal projects exempt from the moratorium.
deck: DOE says the plan is intended to balance power reliability with the country's renewable-energy and climate targets.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Energy Undersecretary Rowena Cristina Guevara said the DOE is preparing a coal transition plan that will include a work program for coal projects not covered by the country's moratorium on new greenfield coal plants.
She estimated that roughly 3,000 to 5,000 MW of previously committed coal capacity remains legally able to proceed, although many projects have not moved into construction.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The Philippines imposed a moratorium on new greenfield coal plants in 2020, while exempting projects already committed before the policy took effect. The government is also targeting a higher renewable-energy share in the power mix.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The policy could influence electricity reliability, investment decisions, power prices and the pace of the country's energy transition. It also raises questions about how near-term supply security will be balanced against long-term emissions goals.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The key document is the final DOE transition plan: its project list, deadlines, treatment of stalled contracts and how it aligns with renewable-energy targets.
